touches.text: Postgres itself is a host service, installed and upgraded by Recovery (6.3.5); Rescue when it won't start.

Every box runs its own instance of the database proxy, and everything on that box talks only to it (4.3.1.5.1.4.1.1). Each box's proxy is its own instance (1.3.4), so this agrees with 5.5.3.8 ("a device runs on one box"): no instance is duplicated, the class has one instance per box, like the foundational set of 5.5.3.8.1. WHY: the local read is fast, and the cache it fills is every box's backup. -amm; the fit with 5.5.3.8 - akienasus_cc_0
Its sockets dial only its own box's Postgres on loopback, never the inference host, so it stands on the sole-path allowed list (11.4.1, 17.13) beside web_operator and usage. - CC

When a client's loopback dial to the proxy is refused (no socket on the box), the client wakes the proxy once through the bus (database start) and retries for up to 60 s. Any other failure, or a wake that fails, is raised at once and names why. WHY: the command lazy-inits the system (5.8.3.2.1), and after a reboot nothing else starts the proxy. - CC
A device owns its state: only the device writes under its own ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/ tree.
The shim always starts its device. Nothing else does.
It wakes the device when it's not running and is needed.
It answers what it can itself; when it can't (eg a health question it holds no answer to), it wakes the device and asks.

A device may declare an idle time; the shim stops it after that long unused, and the next message wakes it again. With none declared it runs until `stop`. WHY: idle costs memory, not CPU, so the librarian, slow to load, stays warm for hours, while something cheap can stop after a minute.
Processes all messages from the bus for its device.

A seal is host independent: one record per proof, whichever box asks. Seals are made by one sealing machine in the cairn device, and there is only ever one cairn (until a laptop dies and a backup takes over), so there is one sealer. A box that is not cairn's home asks the sealer instead of writing its own seal.
